title: How To Improve Behavior By Doing This One Thing
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin identifies communication as the often-missing ingredient for teachers who feel they're doing everything right yet still sense friction with their students. Drawing on his coaching practice, he distills students' core informational needs into three questions: what's next, how long will it take, and why are we doing it. When these questions go unanswered, students feel disconnected and passive, which fuels frustration, excitability, and weakened motivation. He recommends giving a brief preview covering all three at every transition, arguing this makes students feel respected and in control, and functions as one of the simplest, most effective antidotes to common classroom misbehavior.
points: Identifies communication as the frequently overlooked missing piece for teachers who otherwise do everything right but sense subtle friction.
Distills students' core informational needs into three questions: what's next, how long will it take, and why are we doing it.
Argues that leaving these questions unanswered causes students to feel disconnected, passive, frustrated, and less motivated.
Recommends giving a brief preview covering all three questions at every classroom transition.
Frames answering these questions as making students feel respected, in control, and more willing to cooperate.
quotes: So I’ve broken down what students need to feel safe and ready to learn into three simple questions.
1. What’s next? 2. How long will it take? 3. Why are we doing it?
Whenever students are unsure or in the dark about any one or more of these, they begin to feel disconnected, as if education is being done to them rather than being an active participant.
It makes them feel that they’re important, respected, and tethered to the classroom.
Knowing how long eliminates anxiousness so they can listen and concentrate. And knowing why causes them to agree with and go along with your plans.
We free them to enjoy learning and being part of our classroom.
